builds.title: Console Home cards: card@1 asset plugins carry, Home detects/shows/hides every card (always rendered), card layouts, cards for every data plugin
builds.detail:
Brett, Oct 29 2026: "Design a bunch more cards for the console home screen. If plugins with data or dynamic content don't have a card, design one for them from scratch (you decide what to display and how). Plugins can now carry cards that can be designed in the future SDK and attached to the plugin as assets. Console Home detects all card assets attached to plugins and shows or hides them, but always rendered. The card layout can show or hide all cards detected."

Decisions (cards): profile Angel (new, this is its first build; nothing built in the asking session); Fable contract first, then Opus.
Card designs: one per plugin with data/dynamic content (31 plugins + 5 existing Home cards). No card: _template, basic-filter, plugin-switches, plugins-menu (tools with no data of their own).
Clash check Oct 29: no open build touches Home or cards (refactor profile all complete; main-framework pending items unrelated).

steps.text: card@1 asset type in framework/schemas/asset-types.json (+ axf schemas): id, owner (plugin id or "console"), title, icon, kind (stat | list | meter | chart | feed | status | actions | custom), size (s | m | l | wide | tall), data {service (plugin_services capability), path, refreshSec, live:boolean}, slots (headline, value, sub, rows, sparkline, actions), emptyState, actions (ids run through the action engine), level (Simple/Basic/Developer/Administrator), minRole (UAC), defaultVisible, order, category. Open registry: unknown kinds render the custom slot, never fail.

plugin@1 gets `cards: ["cards/<id>.json", …]` (card assets ship inside the plugin folder, so plugin-lifecycle@1 removes them on uninstall); plugin-inventory@1 engine lists each plugin's cards (framework/core/engines/plugins.ts + server/engine.py twin) so anything can detect them; future card SDK attaches cards to a plugin by writing this list.

home-cards@1 engine (TS reference, framework/core/engines/cards.ts): collects every card from enabled plugins + console-owned cards, applies saved visibility/order/size, level and role; hidden cards stay in the output with `hidden: true` so Home ALWAYS renders (mounts) every card and only hides it (instant show, data kept warm). Fixture spec/fixtures/home-cards.json; Kotlin twin recorded as a deferred gap in PORTING.md (Android on hold).

card-layout@1 asset type: columns per window class (compact/medium/expanded), gap + density tokens, grouping (none | plugin | category), "show all / hide all" default, sort (manual | category | plugin). 3 starter layouts: grid-auto, two-column-dashboard, compact-list. Hot-swap via runtime.swap('card-layout', id); tokens only (THEMING.md).

Placeholders for the future card SDK: `axf.cards@1` capability service (list/register/unregister cards at runtime), extension point `home.cards`, typed NotImplemented card designer entry, so a designer plugin can later author card assets and attach them to any plugin without kernel changes.

Home renders from the home-cards engine. The 5 cards already there become console-owned card assets: Plan summary, Build summary, Coverage, Project, Recent installs & imports. Same look at the default theme.

Card layout toolbar on Home (hideable): Show all · Hide all · layout picker (card-layout assets) · group by · a Cards checklist popover with one switch per detected card. Right-click a card: Hide card · Card size · Open plugin · Plugin settings. Drag to reorder. Saved per user in settings (synced through axHub like the rest).
Settings → Home cards tab (with the level toolbar rule): every detected card grouped by plugin, switch + size + order, layout default; a card whose plugin is disabled shows greyed "plugin off".

Cards — Build orchestrator: next step + model chip, approvals waiting (one-tap), phase progress bar per open build. Build manager: remaining work split Fable/Opus, hours + cost left, top 3 builds. Build profiles: active profile chip + pending/queue/orchestrator counts for each profile, switch button.

Cards — Feature matrix: kept vs skipped minutes per build, matrices with unapplied changes (Apply button). Fable rebuilds: parked count, Fable hours left, next rebuild. Changes & features grid: latest 5 changes/features with state dots.

Cards — Codebase changes: live/running entries with heartbeat age and current step. Activity: running/queued CI runs and deploys as a feed. Push banner: branches not on main per repo with PR CI dots. Main build status: last main CI result + sparkline of the last 10 runs.

Cards — Approvals: calls waiting with title + one-tap Approve/Deny, veto countdowns. Systems check: pass/warn/fail meter + top 3 issues with Auto fix. Alerts bell: unread by source (CI, deploys, builds, crashes). Claude badge: AI connection state, active model, last check time.

Cards — AI assistant: live sessions + last message, Open chat. Agent manager: agents (Mosses, Vinny, Molly…) with running/idle state. Molly guide: recent walkthroughs + Ask Molly. AI keys: active key per kind (masked) and how many saved.

Cards — Todo manager: overdue / due today / open by list, quick add. Voice notes: listener state + latest 3 notes. Session check-in: active Claude sessions with machine and repo. Snapshot manager: latest snapshots with one-tap Restore.

Cards — Plugin Manager: enabled/disabled/unhealthy counts. Plugin Update: updates available (Update all). Container access: master switch state + containers up/down. axHub sync: red/green live badge (hubLive rule), last sync. MCP client: connected servers + tool counts.

Cards — Brand library: logo of the day (animated, tap to roll). Theme manager: current colour/style/layout + Roll button. Context menu designer: saved menus + chunks count. Project wizard: recent projects. Claude handoff: kit freshness. Terminal: open tabs and their connections. Feature assistant: last drafted features.

Lifecycle: every plugin's cards/ listed in plugin.json and removed by uninstall.mjs --all; plugin-lifecycle check --after-uninstall for each touched plugin; theme checks (check-theme, theme-swap) over every card.

Tests (engine vs fixture, hidden cards stay mounted, show/hide all, plugin off), docs (_claude/memory/docs/home-cards.md, plugins README → Cards, STATUS), before/after Home screenshots at 412 and 1280 px, re-bake console.

builds.title: Settings redesign: short lists you tap into, dropdowns instead of button walls, tight spacing (starts the whole-app de-clutter)
builds.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice, then 'Go' in text): the app takes up way too much space; Settings is a wall of buttons. Packs only reskin; fix how the screens are built. Agreed plan: settings as short lists you tap into (like phone settings), dropdowns instead of rows of buttons, tight spacing everywhere; start with Settings and show before/after screenshots. Profile: Angel. Layouts stay as they are (Brett: 'Nah' to new layouts). Web first; Android twin of the settings renderer recorded as deferred (Android hold).

steps.text: Before screenshots of every Settings page (phone + desktop) and a list of what wastes space
Settings home = a short list of sections you tap into (phone: one list, back arrow; desktop: list left, page right); plugin settings as one list under Plugins
Choices with more than 3 options become one dropdown; 2–3 options stay a small segmented control; toggles are compact rows
Tight rows: label and control on one line, description under an info tap; groups are plain headed lists, not big cards
Appearance: every asset picker (design pack, style pack, themes, layout…) becomes a compact dropdown row with a small preview instead of a wall of cards/buttons
Level toolbar shrinks to one dropdown; checks (tsc, controls, theme, theme-swap, menu-reach); after screenshots; report + LOG; PR

builds.title: Plugin manifest field 'floatable': can the plugin open as a floating window
builds.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): a field in plugin manifests that declares whether the plugin is floatable, like 'tabable'. Profile: Angel.

steps.text: plugin@1 `floatable`: false (default) | true (its first page) | {view, label, icon, width, height}; schema, plugins.mjs --check and the console loader validate it like `tabable`; PORTING note (Android deferred)

Console honours it: 'Open floating' on the plugin's menu entries, right-click and Plugin Manager opens the view in a floating window (window host); set floatable on every plugin with a page; checks; PR

builds.title: Compact the whole app: tight page heads, smaller buttons and chips, flat cards, dense tables and grids, slimmer banners and toolbars
builds.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026: after the compact Settings (PR #175) — 'Rest of the app too'. Same treatment everywhere: less wasted space, no walls of big buttons, no cards inside cards, tight spacing. Framework-wide (axf.css + console.css), so every app on the framework and every plugin follows; per-screen fixes after. Before/after screenshots of every main screen. Profile: Angel. Web; Android deferred.

notes.text: First pass: framework frame + count strips + Plugin Manager phone layout. Per-screen button walls (orchestrator filters, catalog, tracker, asset studio) left for a follow-up pass.

steps.text: Before screenshots of the main screens (Home, Builds pages, Plugin Manager, Catalog, Assets, Tracker, Build Breaker, Feature matrix, Design packs) phone + desktop

Framework frame in axf.css: page head (smaller title, quiet eyebrow, actions on one line), buttons (padding, size, icon size), chips (small square-ish), segmented, tabs, fields, cards (one border, smaller padding, no dashed outlines), tables/grid rows — tokens only
Chrome: banner, tab bar, application menu bar and toolbars slimmer; Home stat tiles and summary cards dense
Screens with button walls (orchestrator tiles + filter chips, plugin manager cards, catalog, tracker, asset studio): fold extra actions into ⋯ menus or dropdowns, compact lists
Checks (tsc, controls, theme, theme-swap, menu-reach, plugin pages), re-bake apps (Patches skipped), after screenshots, report + LOG, PR

builds.title: UI Review: one plugin where Brett approves every UI a build makes (Design packs renamed and widened)
builds.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice, driving): rename the Design packs console plugin to UI Review (folder ui-review) and make it one all-in-one UI approval plugin. Every UI a build makes is submitted there for his approval, separated by kind (open registry: Design packs, Whole apps / programs, Screens & pages, Settings interfaces, Dialogs & popups, Menus & toolbars, Banners & cards, Other). Items: title, kind, app, build/branch/PR, desktop + phone shots, notes, status (waiting / approved / changes asked / rejected), his comment, history. Views: tree, collapsible grid, grid with sub-grids, gallery, compare; multi-select + bulk decisions in every view. Builds submit through review.mjs, the plugin API and rebuild-shots --submit; capability ui-review@1. Design-pack picks (MAX 3) migrate. Profile: Angel. Web only.

steps.text: Rename: new folder ui-review (plugin.json, install/uninstall, hooks), move packs/, migrate picks from the old data folder, drop the old folder + README line; View → Design packs stays as a shortcut
Data model review-item@1 + open kinds registry (kinds.json), pure core (filters, sort waiting-first, grouping, counts, bulk decisions, history) shared by web, CLI and tests
Server routes (items, submit, decide, bulk, shots, picks, state per branch/PR) + capability ui-review@1 via plugin_services
review.mjs CLI (submit / list / decide / state) and rebuild-shots.mjs --submit option
Web UI: page head, section strip with counts, filters/search/sort, bulk bar; tree + collapsible grid views
Web UI: grid with sub-grids, gallery, compare, item detail (shots, notes, comment, history), Design packs section with Pick flow
Tests (test.py, test.mts) + tsc, vite build, check-theme, check-controls, check-plugin-pages, plugin-lifecycle check, menu-reach
Screenshots of every view (rebuild-shots.mjs), rule line in shared RULES.md, THREADS + push-banner follow-up note, PR through the push banner
Follow-up (after the push-banner build lands): the batch merge holds PRs whose ui-review@1 state is waiting or rejected
